glosses: Plonger dans l’eau ou dans tout autre liquide, voire tout autre gaz.

examples.text: Immerger un tuyau dans l’eau. — Un câble immergé sous l'Atlantique.

glosses: Se plonger dans une occupation ou dans une activité.

examples.text: Entreprendre une méharée au Mali, c'est s'immerger complètement dans le monde du désert, des espaces sans fin, des bivouacs étoilés, des feux de camp et des théières fumantes.
Après un gigot flageolets avalé chez belle-maman, qu'il appelle « ma mère », monsieur met à profit l'après-midi dominical pour s'immerger dans la comptabilité familiale.

translations.source_sense_description: (Didactique) Plonger dans l’eau ou dans tout autre liquide, voire tout autre gaz.

glosses: To place within a fluid (generally a liquid, but also a gas).

examples.text: Archimedes determined the volume of objects by immersing them in water.
... the two plates of platinum immersed in oxygen and hydrogen gases
Even after the process of germination has taken place, if the young plant be immersed in an atmosphere of either of those gases [hydrogen and nitrogen], vegetation and life will immediately cease.
The buoyant force of the atmospheric air on solids and liquids immersed in it is for most purposes negligible compared to the weight of solid or liquid, ...
The sculptor immersed himself in anatomic studies.
Thus, in mathematical terms a Klein bottle cannot be "embedded" but only "immersed" in three dimensions as an embedding has no self-intersections but an immersion may have them.
After a long enquiry of things immerse in matter, I interpose some object which is immateriate, or less materiate; such as this of sounds.

translations.source_sense_description: (Didactique) Plonger dans l’eau ou dans tout autre liquide, voire tout autre gaz.

examples.text: The submarine submerged in the water.

glosses: To put into a liquid; to immerse; to plunge into and keep in.

examples.text: In films, many people are murdered by being submerged in swimming pools.

glosses: To be below the surface of the sea, a lake, river, etc.

examples.text: On the day of RAIL 's site visit, in heavy weather, the scaffolding and decking that engineers stand on were submerged deep under choppy water, with work suspended. "We have to work around the tides," explained Project Director Alan Venables. "The wind pushes the tide up and the waves get larger. That causes some problems with the scaffold."
Because of the death of his father, he is submerged in sorrow.
Mrs Dibble made for the kitchen, stumping violently with her crutches and heaving her bulk along with the obvious determination to submerge her wrongs by resorting to the gin-bottle.
